description: Every constructor is counted, and constructors with no standings records get a count of 0. The average count per constructor is computed over all constructors.

c.request: How many constructor standings records does each constructor have, and how does that compare with the average per constructor? Show the 10 constructors furthest above the average. Give the constructor id, its nationality, its number of standings records, and the difference from the average, largest first. Every constructor is counted, and constructors with no standings records get a count of 0. The average count per constructor is computed over all constructors.
c.sql: WITH standings_count AS (SELECT c.constructorId, c.nationality, COUNT(cs.constructorStandingsId) as standing_count FROM constructors c LEFT JOIN constructorStandings cs ON c.constructorId = cs.constructorId GROUP BY c.constructorId, c.nationality), avg_count AS (SELECT AVG(standing_count) as avg_standing_count FROM standings_count) SELECT sc.constructorId, sc.nationality, sc.standing_count, (sc.standing_count - ac.avg_standing_count) as difference_from_avg FROM standings_count sc CROSS JOIN avg_count ac WHERE (sc.standing_count - ac.avg_standing_count) > 0 ORDER BY difference_from_avg DESC LIMIT 10

b.request: Count constructorStandings records for each constructor including those with zero records, calculate the average count across all constructors in the database, and display the 10 constructors with the highest difference above that average along with their id, nationality, record count, and difference from average.
b.sql: WITH constructor_counts AS (SELECT c.constructorId, c.nationality, COUNT(cs.constructorStandingsId) as record_count FROM constructors c LEFT JOIN constructorStandings cs ON c.constructorId = cs.constructorId GROUP BY c.constructorId, c.nationality), average_calc AS (SELECT AVG(record_count) as avg_count FROM constructor_counts) SELECT cc.constructorId, cc.nationality, cc.record_count, cc.record_count - ac.avg_count as difference_from_average FROM constructor_counts cc CROSS JOIN average_calc ac ORDER BY difference_from_average DESC LIMIT 10
b.raw: Count constructorStandings records for each constructor including those with zero records, calculate the average count across all constructors in the database, and display the 10 constructors with the highest difference above that average along with their id, nationality, record count, and difference from average.

d.request: Count constructorStandings records per constructor including those with zero records, compute the average count across all constructors, return the 10 constructors with the highest count above this average, displaying constructor id, nationality, record count, and difference from average in descending order by difference.
d.sql: WITH constructor_counts AS (SELECT c.constructorId, c.nationality, COUNT(cs.constructorStandingsId) as record_count FROM constructors c LEFT JOIN constructorStandings cs ON c.constructorId = cs.constructorId GROUP BY c.constructorId, c.nationality), avg_count AS (SELECT AVG(record_count) as avg_record_count FROM constructor_counts) SELECT cc.constructorId, cc.nationality, cc.record_count, cc.record_count - ac.avg_record_count as difference_from_average FROM constructor_counts cc CROSS JOIN avg_count ac WHERE cc.record_count > ac.avg_record_count ORDER BY difference_from_average DESC LIMIT 10

a.request: Considering every constructor, with a count of 0 for those that have no constructor standings records, count each constructor's standings records. Compare each count with the average count over all constructors. Show the 10 constructors furthest above that average: the constructor id, its `nationality`, its record count, and the difference from the average (unrounded), largest difference first.
a.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT c.constructorId, c.nationality, COUNT(cs.constructorStandingsId) as record_count FROM constructors c LEFT JOIN constructorStandings cs ON c.constructorId = cs.constructorId GROUP BY c.constructorId, c.nationality) SELECT constructorId, nationality, record_count, record_count - (SELECT AVG(record_count) FROM counts) as difference FROM counts WHERE record_count > (SELECT AVG(record_count) FROM counts) ORDER BY difference DESC LIMIT 10
